entities.evidence: The heading introduces the family of Noah, Lamech’s son, whose sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth are named in Genesis 6:10.
The repeated name identifies the Noah of the family heading as the righteous man.
The final occurrence names the same Noah as the subject of “walked with God.”

analysis.evidence: In אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ (“These are the generations of Noah”), אֵלֶּה is the subject of a verbless clause. It points forward to the account of Noah that follows.
analysis.morphology: Common plural demonstrative pronoun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ, the construct noun takes נֹחַ as its complement. The phrase introduces Noah’s family history, and the account begins by describing Noah himself.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: generations, the account of what came from someone

analysis.evidence: In אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ, “these are the generations of Noah,” the marked name completes the construct phrase תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ and identifies whose generations are introduced.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ (“These are the generations of Noah”), the marked נֹחַ names the subject of the next clause, which describes Noah as אִישׁ צַדִּיק (“a righteous man”).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In נֹחַ אִישׁ צַדִּיק, “Noah was a righteous man,” אִישׁ identifies Noah as a man. The adjective צַדִּיק supplies the description “righteous.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אִישׁ צַדִּיק describes Noah as “a righteous man.” The verse also calls him תָּמִים (“blameless”) and says that he walked with God.
analysis.morphology: Adjective, masculine singular absolute, modifying אִישׁ.
analysis.sense: righteous (of a man): doing right before God

analysis.evidence: תָּמִים הָיָה בְּדֹרֹתָיו describes Noah as blameless among his contemporaries. The verse calls him אִישׁ צַדִּיק, “a righteous man,” and says that he walked with God. Both descriptions support a sense of integrity in his conduct.
analysis.morphology: Adjective, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with הָיָה.

analysis.evidence: In תָּמִים הָיָה בְּדֹרֹתָיו, הָיָה links Noah to the adjective תָּמִים: he was blameless in his generations.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Noah. The phrase תָּמִים הָיָה בְּדֹרֹתָיו describes him as blameless among the people of the generations in which he lived.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ (in, among) + masculine plural construct noun דֹרֹת + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ָיו (his).
analysis.sense: generation, the people alive at one time

analysis.evidence: In אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים הִתְהַלֶּךְ נֹחַ, “Noah walked with God,” נֹחַ is the subject of הִתְהַלֶּךְ. The verb is intransitive here, and אֶת introduces הָאֱלֹהִים as Noah’s companion.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים הִתְהַלֶּךְ נֹחַ, אֶת means “with” and identifies God as the one with whom Noah walked.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + masculine plural noun in the absolute state, singular in sense.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים הִתְהַלֶּךְ נֹחַ, Noah is the subject and אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים means “with God.” The preceding description of Noah as צַדִּיק and תָּמִים shows that walking with God describes his way of life.
analysis.morphology: Hithpael perfect, third person masculine singular
analysis.sense: conduct one’s life in fellowship with God
